question: The price of an article increases by 20% every year. If the difference between its price at the end of the third and that of the fourth year is ₹86.40, then its price (in ₹) at the end of the second year is:
solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the initial cost of the article be 100.

⇒ Price of article after 1st year = 1.2 × 100 = 120

⇒ Price of article after 2nd year = 1.2 × 120 = 144

⇒ Price of article after 3rd year = 1.2 × 144 = 172.8

⇒ Price of article after 4th year = 1.2 × 178 = 207.36

Difference in the cost after the third and fourth years = 207.36 - 172.8 = 34.56

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/315a0619cafdd33389c22c61adb038b160c4bb5daee915191ccb6733845d86b1.png] 

⇒ x = 86.4× 100over34.56 = Rs 250

Price at the end of the second year = 1.2 × 1.2 × 250 = Rs 360

**∴ The price at the end of the second year is Rs 360.**
